newsitem.title: USA: IBP Inc says cutting back pork production.
newsitem.headline: IBP Inc says cutting back pork production.

text.p: IBP Inc on Thursday announced it was making "significant" cutbacks in production at virtually all its seven pork plants this week and next.
"All IBP pork facilites are operating at less than 40 hours this week and all but one plant will operate at 32 hours next week," spokesman Gary Mickelson said.
"The company expects to process 33,000 less hogs than expected the remainder of this week and 59,000 to 60,000 less hogs than anticipated through next week," Mickelson said.
Operating margins were the problem and IBP could not currently move its pork products at prices high enough to offset the higher cost of live hogs, Mickelson said.
IBP's pork plants are in Columbus Junction, Council Bluffs, Perry, Storm Lake and Waterloo, all in Iowa, Madison, Nebraska and Logansport, Indiana.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog prices near midday were quoted up $0.50 per cwt, with a top of $56.00, according to USDA.
